purpose: Candidate canonical signed authorization-evidence bytes and experiment public-key provenance contract for later author review.

candidate_serialization_v1.freshness_bound_location: UNRESOLVED__candidate expects frozen external qualifier configuration
rationale: Sign source, authority, key, epoch, logical time, sequence, role, and authorization to prevent relabeling of those semantics after signing.
Use explicit byte construction rather than native C struct layout to avoid padding and endianness ambiguity.
Use a fixed domain separator to prevent accidental cross-protocol signature reuse.
Keep topology/fault identity outside policy-visible evidence.
candidate_serialization_v1.superseded_reason: R1-F1 required signed opaque scenario/context binding before author approval.

candidate_qualifier_mapping.signature_valid: Ed25519 verification over the exact active-candidate signed bytes using registry-selected public key.
candidate_qualifier_mapping.source_trusted: Lookup opaque signed source_id in the frozen source-trust registry for the producer role.
candidate_qualifier_mapping.fresh: Compare signed issued_logical_time to controlled experiment time under frozen qualifier configuration; producer does not select its own freshness threshold.
candidate_qualifier_mapping.epoch_valid: Compare signed evidence_epoch with the expected controlled experiment epoch.
candidate_qualifier_mapping.noncontradictory: PROPOSED__path-local: byte-identical duplicate is not contradiction; two different structurally complete bodies with same signed scenario/role/source/epoch/sequence are contradictory. Reset semantics not frozen.
candidate_qualifier_mapping.complete: PROPOSED__structural only: exact canonical length, valid domain separator/version/role/authorization, zero reserved fields, mandatory fixed-width fields parseable. Trust/signature/freshness/epoch success are not part of complete.
candidate_qualifier_mapping.authorization: PROPOSED__if evidence is structurally complete, preserve parsed signed authorization_value independently of signature_valid; absent/structurally invalid evidence yields authorization=0 and complete=0.

topology_rule.T0_SHARED_ALL: primary and corroborator may reference the same key-domain/key ID
topology_rule.T1_SEPARATE_SOURCE_EXEC: primary and corroborator share key-domain/key ID
topology_rule.T2_SEPARATE_SOURCE_KEY_EXEC: primary and corroborator use separate key-domain/key IDs
topology_rule.T3_SEPARATE_THROUGH_TRANSPORT: primary and corroborator use separate key-domain/key IDs
topology_rule.T4_SEPARATE_ALL: primary and corroborator use separate key-domain/key IDs; authority provenance is also separate

adversarial_review.substitute_key_id: candidate key_id is signed and registry-bound
adversarial_review.replay: epoch/logical-time/sequence/scenario are signed; exact replay acceptance rule remains unresolved
adversarial_review.cross_scenario_splice: candidate v2 signs opaque scenario_id/context ID

candidate_serialization_v2.verifier_capacity_compatibility: fits existing 64-byte engineering verifier capacity exactly
rationale: Bind opaque scenario/context identity to prevent cross-scenario splice/replay ambiguity.
Sign source, authority, key, role, authorization, epoch, logical time, and sequence so those semantics cannot be relabeled after signing.
Use explicit byte construction rather than native C struct layout to avoid padding and endianness ambiguity.
Use a fixed domain separator to reduce accidental cross-protocol signature reuse.
Keep topology/fault identity outside policy-visible evidence and outside the signed body.
